title: Chicken breast, baked, broiled, or roasted with marinade, skin eaten, from raw

content.title: About
content.content: Chicken breast is a lean cut of poultry meat, high in protein and low in calories. When cooked with a flavorful marinade and the skin left on, it stays juicy and gains additional taste from herbs and spices.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Chicken breast provides almost twice the protein of most red‑meat cuts.
Marinating helps retain moisture and enhances flavor, especially for baking or grilling.
The skin is rich in collagen, which can be beneficial for skin and joint health when cooked properly.
Traditional oven roasting is done at 180‑200 °C for about 20‑25 minutes, depending on thickness.
When grilling, removing the skin beforehand reduces fat content if a low‑fat diet is desired.

items.title: High protein content
items.content: A 100‑g serving delivers roughly 31 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Low fat
items.content: Skin‑less chicken breast contains less than 3 g of fat per 100 g, making it suitable for low‑fat diets.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B3 (niacin) and B6 aid energy metabolism and nervous‑system function.

items.title: Contains essential minerals
items.content: Chicken provides phosphorus, selenium and zinc, important for bones, immunity and antioxidant defense.

items.title: Promotes satiety
items.content: The combination of high protein and moderate calories helps keep you feeling full longer.

items.title: Food‑borne illness risk
items.content: Raw chicken may harbor Salmonella or Campylobacter; cook to an internal temperature of 74 °C to ensure safety.

items.title: Poultry allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to chicken proteins and should avoid consumption.

items.title: Sodium in marinades
items.content: Commercial marinades can be high in salt; choose low‑sodium or homemade versions if sodium intake is a concern.

items.title: Potential carcinogen formation
items.content: High‑heat grilling can create heterocyclic amines; cook at moderate temperatures and avoid charring.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Marinate the breast in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and herbs, then bake, broil, or grill until the internal temperature reaches 74 °C. The skin can be left on for extra flavor or removed before serving. Serve with vegetables, whole grains, or slice for salads.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep raw chicken breast refrigerated at +1‑4 °C for up to 2 days, or freeze at ‑18 °C for up to 9 months. Cooked breast should be stored in an airtight container in the fridge for 3‑4 days.
